headline: The runtime floor moves to Node.js 24.21.0 and OpenSSL 3.5.8
summary: OpenSSL 3.5.8 is a security patch release fixing ten flaws, the most severe rated Moderate. The runtime floor moves to Node.js 24.21.0, which carries that release along with root certificates from NSS 3.126. The vendored framework moves to blamejs 0.19.7, and the container bases and workflow action pins are brought current.

items.title: Runtime floor raised to Node.js 24.21.0 for OpenSSL 3.5.8
items.body: OpenSSL 3.5.8 is a security patch release fixing ten flaws, the most severe rated Moderate. Among them are a double free and unbounded memory growth in the QUIC server (CVE-2026-18798, CVE-2026-14456), a heap buffer overflow in CMS key unwrapping (CVE-2026-63072), an invalid pointer dereference in the CMP server (CVE-2026-63076), a dereference of a missing certificate in RPK signature-algorithm selection (CVE-2026-14457), and excessive memory use buffering DTLS records for a future epoch (CVE-2026-54874). This client uses TLS 1.3 over TCP and does not use the QUIC, DTLS, CMS or CMP surfaces those fixes cover. The floor moves so that the runtime embedded in the release binaries carries the patched library.

items.title: Root certificates move to NSS 3.126
items.body: The client seeds its certificate authority bundle from the runtime's compiled-in root store, because supplying a bundle replaces Node's default trust rather than adding to it. Node 24.21.0 carries the NSS 3.126 root set, two updates on from the NSS 3.123.1 set in 24.19.0. Both the sync transport and the update downloader trust that set.

items.title: Node.js 24.21.0 is the declared floor
items.body: The boot check, the container image, and the continuous-integration matrix move together. Pre-built binaries embed their own runtime and are unaffected by the version installed on the machine. A from-source install on Node.js 24.20.x or older now exits at startup with the version it needs.

items.title: Vendored framework moves to blamejs 0.19.7
items.body: The framework renamed its error codes from bare names to a namespaced form, and this client's matches on them move with it: the update downloader's HTTP-status branch, the log sink's symlink refusal, and the encrypted-session reset and retry. The wire formats this client shares with a HermitStash server are unchanged, so it still works against a server on the 0.18 line.

items.title: A WebSocket connection with no resolved address now reports ENOTFOUND
items.body: When the request filter resolved a host to an empty address list, the WebSocket client continued to dial and surfaced whatever the socket layer reported. It now fails with ENOTFOUND naming the host, and the reconnect loop retries it as a transient failure.

items.title: Container bases and action pins brought current
items.body: The build-stage Node image and the Chainguard runtime base are re-pinned to the digests current at this release, and every action the workflows call is pinned to the commit of its latest release.
